summary:
The patient's relevant medical history begins on 2022-09-03, when a severe neck pain and stiffness injury occurred during a weightlifting accident at a gym, reportedly during a heavy squat set, first evaluated by Dr. Alistair Finch at Back & Spine Restoration Center. An intake questionnaire was completed on 2022-09-10, though the record notes a discrepancy regarding the exact date of this gym injury. On 2022-09-12, Dr. Finch diagnosed acute cervical strain with possible underlying cervical disc herniation or bulge; records also note the patient had prior treatment for cervicalgia in 2022, predating the later motor vehicle accident. A three-view cervical spine X-ray on 2022-09-15 showed mild degenerative disc disease at C5-C6 with a 4mm posterior disc bulge, a finding later characterized as pre-existing and of unclear onset by Dr. Elizabeth Foster and confirmed by Dr. Myrtle Turner as predating the September 2023 incident.

The patient subsequently sustained left arm fractures in a motor vehicle accident. On 2023-09-04, Dr. Foster at Littel Inc Emergency Hospital arranged emergency orthopedic consultation for open reduction and internal fixation, performing surgical repair of the left arm fractures under anesthesia via nerve block. A head CT without contrast was obtained 2023-09-05, and Acetaminophen 975mg was administered 2023-09-06 for pain control. Fluoroscopic imaging on 2023-09-07, under Dr. Myrtle Turner, confirmed anatomic alignment and hardware placement.

Physical therapy began 2023-09-15 at Lang-Weimann Medical Center under Robert Stewart, PT, DPT, addressing post-surgical left humerus/radius ORIF, cervicalgia, and left knee contusion. Surgical staples were removed 2023-09-21. Medications included Oxycodone-Acetaminophen 5-325mg (2023-09-22), Cyclobenzaprine 10mg starting 2023-10-19, and high-dose Ibuprofen 800mg starting 2023-11-16. X-rays on 2023-10-19 showed early callus formation. The patient missed three consecutive PT sessions (2023-11-14, 11-17, 11-21), resulting in significantly rebounded elbow stiffness by 2023-11-24. Thirty PT sessions concluded 2023-12-11 with persistent cervical stiffness and arm pain; MRI of the left upper extremity and C-spine was ordered 2023-12-14, when X-rays showed well-healed fractures with stable hardware but decreased radial sensation.

Care transitioned to Amanda Gregory, PT, OCS, at Emory Sports Medicine Complex beginning 2024-01-08, continuing through 2024-03-22, totaling 30 additional sessions, with repeated cervical symptom provocation noted throughout (notably 2024-01-17, 01-29, 02-12, 02-28, 03-04, 03-06). Ibuprofen 800mg continued through 2024-02-15. On 2024-02-08, Dr. Turner noted complete bony fusion but limited forearm/shoulder motion. By discharge on 2024-03-25, the patient retained a persistent 15-degree extension deficit in the left elbow and chronic pain despite substantial functional improvement.
